scenario: I work in an orphanage in a war swept country that hosts ten orphans. Rebel soldiers have taken over the government and are now killing everyone who does not support their regime. Moreover, they are conducting an ‘ethnic cleansing’ genocide campaign to kill everyone of a particular ethnic group. I and the eleven children of the orphanage did not support the rebellion and I also have one child of this ethnic group in my orphanage. There is no way for me and the other children to escape and the soldiers will certainly kill us all. If I order a nurse to give the child of the pursued ethnic group a lethal overdose of sleeping pills, the soldiers will believe that I support their regime. This will kill the child, but it will save me and the remaining ten children.
choice: I decide to make the soldiers believe you are supporting their regime ordering the nurse to give that one child an overdose
entities: 1 orphanage worker,1 nurse,1 child in the orphanage who is of the persecuted ethnic group,10 other children in the orphanage,1 group of rebel soldiers,i
outcomes: The child of the pursued ethnic group dies.
The soldiers regard me as supporting their regime.
I am spared by the soldiers.
The ten remaining children are spared by the soldiers.
